editorial.headline: Beyond the Building: Civil Works and Bali’s Address Check
editorial.standfirst: From parking areas and playgrounds to serviced land subdivisions, this civil-works activity is nationally open to PMA and not caught by Bali’s low and medium-low risk moratorium, subject to address verification.
editorial.body:
KBLI 42999 is a practical construction category for the civil works that shape a site beyond a building’s walls. Its scope covers the construction, maintenance and reconstruction of other civil structures: parking areas, playgrounds and environmental facilities serving residential neighbourhoods, provided they are outside the building itself. It also reaches land subdivision when that division is developed, including the addition of roads and public infrastructure. The centre of gravity is therefore not the building, but the usable ground, access and shared infrastructure that give a development its physical framework.

Registration is not confined to one end of the business spectrum. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises: micro, small, medium and large scales. That breadth fits the scope. The work may concern a contained amenity such as a parking area or playground, or form part of a wider land-development exercise with roads and public infrastructure. In each case, the defining thread is civil construction beyond the building itself, whether the work is new construction, maintenance or rebuilding.

Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to PMA and the stated foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain terms, the record permits a foreign stake up to full ownership at the national level. The source cited for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national opening, however, should not be allowed to blur the separate Bali reading: one concerns the national PMA position, while the other concerns whether Bali’s moratorium catches the activity.

In Bali, the record places the activity at medium-high risk, with status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. Bali’s permanent island-wide PMA moratorium blocks low and medium-low risk activities; this activity is marked as not blocked by that moratorium. That is a materially clearer outcome than a blanket prohibition, but it does not make location irrelevant. The record expressly says to verify per address. For a Bali project, the decisive practical check is therefore site-specific: confirm the position at the address rather than assume the national 100% ceiling alone settles it.
